Society & Human Rights
• Australia repatriated IS-linked women and children from Syria, with authorities signaling some adults may face terrorism or slavery-related charges upon arrival. 
• Ukraine is weighing a ban on foreign access to surrogacy, a move that could end its role as a global hub for commercial arrangements. 
• Antisemitism has become a flashpoint in UK regional campaigning, while London’s police watchdog is probing Met officers’ handling of abuse allegations against Mohamed Al Fayed. 
• Rights and policing incidents drew scrutiny: Bolivian police fired tear gas at protesting teachers; Israel opened a probe after a soldier was photographed desecrating a Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon; a US driver was arrested after chasing a child cyclist. 
• Policy and social trends: France expanded €1 student canteen meals nationwide; a US court struck down an FCC anti-discrimination rule; new studies highlight gaps in research on over‑50 dating and risks of sexualized online profiles. 
Why it matters: Social protections, policing standards and migration policies are reshaping debates over safety, rights and inclusion across multiple democracies.

Economy & Markets
• Energy shock: Shell’s Q1 profit jumped to $6.92bn amid Iran-war volatility, even as it warned of lower gas output after Gulf facility damage; Emirates reported record profits despite conflict-related disruptions. 
• Markets swung on geopolitics: oil fell below $100 and stocks rose on hopes of a US‑Iran deal; Japan’s Nikkei hit a record high with SoftBank surging. 
• Supply chains: Maersk warned Iran conflict costs have risen by $500m per month and could persist for months; European jet fuel supply is a summer risk. 
• Policy shifts: Australia will reserve 20% of east-coast gas exports for domestic use to curb prices, drawing industry pushback. 
• Tech-led gains: AMD, Arm and others rode a CPU renaissance; Saudi Arabia’s sovereign fund returned to dollar bonds issuance. 
Why it matters: Energy and geopolitical volatility are filtering through to transport costs, inflation and asset prices, while policy responses and tech momentum are reshaping corporate outlooks.

• Research advances included a promising antimalarial enzyme target and nuanced evidence on red-light therapy benefits. 
Why it matters: Transparent public health communication and steady research pipelines remain crucial as emerging infections and politicized oversight challenge preparedness and trust.

Why it matters: Any Iran de‑escalation could quickly alter regional risk, energy flows and allied politics, while Europe navigates security trade-offs.

Economy & Markets.title: Odd Lots: How a US City Can Become a Manufacturing Hub (Podcast)

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Learn What It Takes to Become a Cybersecurity Consultant
Armed Conflict & Security.text: Cybersecurity consultants have never been more in demand. Information security analyst roles are projected to grow nearly 30 percent between now and 2034, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. More than 15 million cybercrime incidents occurred worldwide in 2024, Statista reported.Data breaches are costly and pose direct safety risks. Statista reported that more than US $10 trillion is spent annually repairing the damage caused by cybercrime, most commonly phishing, spoofing, extortion, and data breaches. In one example in the United States, breathalyzer devices installed in vehicles became disabled, leaving hundreds of drivers stranded, as detailed in an IEEE Spectrum article.To help you acquire the skills you need to distinguish yourself from other cybersecurity job candidates, the IEEE Computer Society offers a “What Makes a Great Cybersecurity Consultant” guide. The 23-page PDF includes hard and soft skills you need, a list of certifications to pursue, and key IEEE cybersecurity conferences for staying updated on developments in the field.The guide includes advice from two cybersecurity experts. John D. Johnson, an IEEE senior member, is the founder and CEO of Aligned Security in Bettendorf, Iowa. Ricardo J. Rodriguez is an associate professor of computer science and systems engineering at the Universidad de Zaragoza, in Spain, who researches digital forensics and other cybersecurity topics.“Technology, remote work, and a shortage of skilled workers make this the ideal time to consider becoming a cybersecurity consultant,” Johnson says in the guide. “Consulting can give you the flexibility, variety, and control over where you want your career to go.”Hard and soft skillsAt a minimum, cybersecurity professionals should have a general understanding of IT including operating systems, communication protocols, network architecture, and programming languages such as C++, Java, and Python. They also should be well-versed in security auditing, firewall management, penetration testing, and encryption technologies.The principles of ethical hacking and coding would be handy as well.“To be able to defend a system well, you first have to know how to attack it,” Rodriguez says.The guide explains that there are now more technologies available to help cybersecurity consultants monitor threats and protect systems. They include security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) platforms, which automate workflows to collect security data, streamline incident response, and automate repetitive tasks.Rodriguez points to advances in domain name system security extensions (DNSSEC), which uses digital signatures based on public-key cryptography to strengthen the authentication of the domain name system. By validating data authenticity, DNSSEC safeguards against attacks such as DNS spoofing and guarantees that users connect to the correct IP address.Technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, and quantum computing will increasingly be used to help thwart cyberattacks, the guide suggests. AI is expected to enhance the quality of data analysis, Rodriguez says.Although hard skills are important, soft skills are just as crucial, according to the guide. Critical thinking, project management, flexibility, teamwork, and organizational and presentation skills are essential.It’s not enough to be good at analyzing security vulnerabilities; you also need to clearly describe the situation and explain possible solutions.“Soft skills are important to achieve good team cohesion,” Rodriguez says, “because consultants often lead diverse teams from within their client’s organization.”“It’s essential,” Johnson adds, “that you demonstrate to clients you’re a team player and a capable communicator, and that you meet your commitments.”Security certificationsPossessing security-specific credentials is a valuable way to demonstrate your expertise to potential clients, according to the guide. Because hundreds of certifications are available, Johnson says, pinpointing the most relevant ones can be challenging. Some people focus on theoretical knowledge, while others want to cover practical applications of technology.“Survey the industry and compare it to your skills,” Johnson recommends. “Decide what you want to do, and identify where you have gaps in your skills and experience.”Here are four of the nine certifications listed in the guide that are frequently cited as being important. All the providers are cybersecurity organizations.Certified information security manager. This globally recognized certification from the ISACA is for professionals managing enterprise information security.Certified cloud security professional. Offered by ISC2, this credential validates advanced technical skills in designing, managing, and securing cloud infrastructure.Certified ethical hacker. This certification from the International Council of E-Commerce Consultants (C-Council) confirms proficiency in using methods commonly employed by malicious hackers to detect vulnerabilities.Offensive security certified professional. A hands-on, 24-hour certification exam offered by OffSec covers practical testing skills.Additional industry-specific certifications might be required for organizations in finance, government, health care, or manufacturing.Sound general knowledge—backed by experience, training, and certification—is an essential foundation for being a specialist, Johnson says.Conferences and networking opportunitiesEvents sponsored by the IEEE Computer Society can help you learn about the latest research and advancements in cybersecurity:IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, from 18 to 21 May in San Francisco.IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy, from 6 to 10 July in Lisbon.IEEE International Conference on Cyber Security and Resilience, from 3 to 5 August in Lisbon.IEEE Secure Development Conference, from 14 to 16 October in Indianapolis.Conferences can give you insight into the field and let you do some networking, but it’s important to network elsewhere as well, experts say. Consider joining the IEEE Technical Community on Security and Privacy, which connects experts and professionals advancing research in areas such as encryption, operating system security, and data privacy.Learning and meeting people keeps your knowledge sharp and can lead to mentorship opportunities with established cybersecurity consultants, Johnson says.Other IEEE resourcesThe IEEE Computer Society’s cybersecurity resources page offers a wealth of information including fundamentals, possible career paths, and standards development. To keep you updated on trends, the society publishes IEEE Transactions on Privacy and the IEEE Security and Privacy magazine.In addition to the guide, the IEEE Learning Network offers nearly 30 courses on cybersecurity. And you can find research papers in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library.

Entertainment.title: It’s a ‘Scooby-Doo’ Reunion: Matthew Lillard Is Joining James Gunn’s ‘Man of Tomorrow’
Entertainment.text: SummaryMatthew Lillard joins the cast of the James Gunn-directed sequel in an undisclosed mystery roleThe production shifts technical gears with Sam McCurdy taking over cinematography dutiesMan of Tomorrow centers on an uneasy alliance between David Corenswet’s Superman and Nicholas Hoult’s Lex LuthorJames Gunn and DC Studios are officially expanding the Man of Steel mythos with the announcement of Matthew Lillard joining the cast of the upcoming Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow.Man of Tomorrow is both a technical expansion of the DCU and a notable cultural reunion, marking 25 years since Lillard and Gunn collaborated on the live-action Scooby-Doo franchise. This hybrid approach to casting sees Lillard joining an ensemble that already includes David Corenswet as the titular hero, Nicholas Hoult as Lex Luthor, and Frank Eidinger. While Lillard's specific character remains under wraps, his inclusion signals a continued "Lillardissance," positioning the actor within one of the most anticipated tentpole releases of the decade.On the technical front, the production is leaning into a fresh visual direction with cinematographer Sam McCurdy (Shōgun) stepping in to lens the sequel. The narrative architecture of the film reportedly pivots away from the origin-story beats of its predecessor, focusing instead on a complex, "uneasy alliance" between Superman and Luthor. This shift in tone suggests a more nuanced, politically charged exploration of Metropolis, grounded by the physical production move to Atlanta’s state-of-the-art facilities.Man of Tomorrow is currently scheduled to hit theaters on July 9, 2027.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Scarlett Johansson Is Entering the Ari Aster Multiverse
Entertainment.text: SummaryScarlett Johansson is set to star in and produce the upcoming A24 feature film titled ScapegoatThe project marks the first collaboration between the Academy Award nominee and visionary director Ari AsterProduction is slated to begin in late 2026 under Aster and Lars Knudsen’s Square Peg production bannerScarlett Johansson is officially set to star in Ari Aster’s newest A24 film, Scapegoat. The project, which is currently slated for a late 2026 production start, pairs the Academy Award nominee with the visionary director behind Hereditary and Midsommar for a project that anchors the next era of Square Peg’s output.Scapegoat is positioned as a significant production milestone for Lars Knudsen’s Square Peg banner, which continues its long-standing partnership with A24. The project’s technical window is currently fixed for late 2026, a logistical timeframe that allows Johansson to navigate a dense schedule featuring upcoming roles in The Exorcist and The Batman Part II. While granular plot details remain strictly under wraps, the title suggests a return to the visceral, character-driven tension that has defined Aster’s directorial legacy.The cultural significance of this union cannot be overstated, as it signals Johansson’s return to the auteur-led indie space she previously navigated in cult favorites like Under the Skin. By blending Aster’s penchant for high-concept dread with Johansson’s prestige-drama gravitas, the film bridges the gap between commercial blockbuster power and the "elevated horror" movementStay tuned for an official trailer and release date.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Kohei Kawatani Frames the Past in Tokyo for Kiko Kostadinov SS26 Accessories
Entertainment.text: SummaryKiko Kostadinov has officially unveiled its Spring/Summer 2026 campaign, captured by long-time brand collaborator and photographer Kohei KawataniShot at his studio on the outskirts of Tokyo, the campaign draws heavy inspiration from the atmospheric, understated qualities of Japan's Showa eraThe imagery creates a visual tension between quiet nostalgia and modern fabrication, highlighting the precise textures and construction of the garmentsA deep sense of quiet nostalgia anchors the newly unveiled Spring/Summer 2026 campaign from Kiko Kostadinov. Expanding upon an ongoing, multi-year collaboration documenting the brand's intricate accessories, acclaimed photographer Kohei Kawatani has now turned his lens toward the full menswear and womenswear collections. Shot entirely at his personal studio on the outskirts of Tokyo, the striking new imagery utilizes a visual language heavily steeped in the atmospheric beauty of Japan's Showa era, allowing Kiko Kostadinov's modern garments to speak volumes against a subdued, timeworn backdrop.Kawatani's approach relies heavily on the distinct visual identity of the Showa period, a time characterized by understated interiors, deeply softened lighting, and a rich material patina. By placing the SS26 collections within this archival-feeling environment, the campaign creates a compelling tension between the past and the present. This juxtaposition perfectly underscores the collection's core ethos: reinterpreting historical cues through cutting-edge textile development and highly technical silhouette engineering.Against the quiet studio setting, the meticulous tactility of the clothing and accessories emerges with striking clarity. Kawatani's consistent photographic discipline deepens the dialogue between the objects and their environment, ensuring that while the menswear and womenswear are presented under a unified visual narrative, every individual piece retains its own distinct, powerful presence.By seamlessly blending historical atmosphere with contemporary design, Kawatani proves once again why his curatorial eye is so essential to the visual identity of Kiko Kostadinov. The SS26 campaign is more than just a seasonal lookbook; it is a thoughtful, cinematic exploration of form, texture, and the enduring power of considered fabrication.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Kim Kardashian’s NikeSKIMS Debuts the Buttery-Soft “Studio Stretch” Collection
Entertainment.text: SummaryThe 11-piece capsule utilizes an ultrasoft fabric blended with Lycra Adaptiv for optimal shape retention and dynamic movementNike’s signature Dri-FIT technology merges with SKIMS’ fit-focused ethos to support both high-intensity studio sessions and daily wearMinimal seam lines and a neutral color palette position the garments as foundational layers within a broader, interconnected wardrobeKim Kardashian’s NikeSKIMS has debuted the Studio Stretch, an ultrasoft fabric engineered specifically for the physical demands of studio environments like yoga and pilates. Moving away from heavy, restrictive compression, the material utilizes Lycra Adaptiv to enhance dynamic stretch, ease of movement, and long-term recovery, ensuring the garments hold their structural shape wear after wear. To handle intense activity, Nike’s proprietary Dri-FIT technology is woven directly into the fabric, actively wicking moisture to keep the wearer dry without sacrificing the buttery-soft, second-skin hand feel.The accompanying Studio Stretch collection is both a hyper-functional performance milestone and a cultural nod to modern athleisure, engineered to shift seamlessly from the yoga mat to the city streets. The release spans 11 distinct silhouettes, ranging from bras, tops, shorts, and leggings to an adjustable, scoop-back one-piece. Construction details are heavily dialed into reducing physical distractions, employing minimal seam lines to eliminate fabric bunching and deliver a smooth profile. Every technical spec, from precise strap placement to contoured waistband shaping, has been meticulously mapped to support a wide range of body types across an XXS to 4X size run.Zooming out, the release is a continuation of the disruptive paradigm shift initiated by the Nike and SKIMS partnership. By marrying Nike's unrivaled athletic innovation with Kim Kardashian’s obsession with fit and the female form, the collection transcends standard gym gear. Designed as a core component of the broader NikeSKIMS "system of dress," the neutral-toned "Studio Stretch" pieces are built to layer effortlessly under the brand's semi-sheer "Weightless" layers or breathable "Airy" basics. It represents a new standard in the industry — garments that function as high-performance technical tools while doubling as everyday foundational essentials for personal expression.The NikeSKIMS "Studio Stretch" collection drops globally on May 14 via NikeSKIMS and SKIMS online, with a wider release at select Nike, SKIMS, and partner retail locations to follow.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Oscar Isaac Is Going All-In on a New Netflix Casino Drama Produced by Martin Scorsese
Entertainment.text: SummaryOscar Isaac stars as Robert “Bobby Red” Redman in a new eight-episode Netflix series set in the modern casino industryThe production marks the launch of a first-look deal between Netflix and Isaac’s production company Mad GeneLegendary filmmaker Martin Scorsese joins the executive production team alongside showrunners Brian Koppelman and David LevienOscar Isaac has officially joined the highly anticipated (yet still untitled) Vegas drama series produced by Martin Scorsese. The Netflix project, which explores the sharp-elbowed business of present-day Las Vegas casinos, serves as the first major title under a new creative partnership between the streamer and Isaac’s Mad Gene production banner.The architectural backbone of the series is built on a heavy-hitting creative lineup led by showrunners Brian Koppelman and David Levien. Known for their work on Billions and Super Pumped, the duo handles writing and executive production duties for the eight-episode season. Structurally, the narrative focuses on Isaac’s character, Robert “Bobby Red” Redman, a casino president forced into high-risk maneuvers to defend his territory in a modernized, dangerous version of the city.The production specifications are further bolstered by director J.C. Chandor, who is tapped to direct the first two episodes. Chandor also joins the executive producer roster, which includes Scorsese via Sikelia Productions, Julie Yorn and Rick Yorn for Expanded Media, Paul Schiff, and Beth Schacter. The series is technically framed as a present-day exploration of the industry, moving away from the period-piece aesthetics often associated with the genre to focus on the contemporary mechanics of the Las Vegas strip.This series is the flagship of a broader business arrangement where Netflix holds first-look rights on film and series projects from Mad Gene, the company Isaac leads with Elvira Lind and Gena Konstantinakos. While the series is currently entering the production phase, it follows a run of high-profile Netflix collaborations for Isaac, including BEEF Season 2 and the forthcoming In the Hand of Dante.The untitled series is currently entering production, with further casting and filming updates expected to follow.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: TELFAR’s Everyday Tote Gets a Heavy-Duty Upgrade With the Utility Bag
Entertainment.text: SummaryCrafted from washed duck canvas, the latest tote features a camouflage twill interior and heavy-duty zipper closuresDeep side gussets offer dedicated space for hydration while the main compartment easily houses a laptopThe highly anticipated drop arrives in versatile Black and Drab colorways complete with screen-printed drawstring packagingTELFAR is upgrading its classic Shopping Bag with the Utility Bag, a tactical evolution of its signature silhouette and a direct response to the everyday needs of its community.Since redefining the modern luxury landscape with its universally recognizable Shopping Bag, TELFAR has maintained a deep dialogue with its audience. Now, the brand is channeling that legacy of accessibility into a rugged, hyper-functional format designed for what it dubs “urban survival.” Swapping out its traditional vegan leather for a heavy-duty, washed duck canvas, the latest release grounds the brand's inclusive ethos in hard-wearing, utilitarian construction.The technical upgrades are deliberate and spec-focused, directly answering long-standing fan requests for increased security and organization. The top is now secured with a full zipper closure, while an adjustable strap provides versatile carry options across any fit. Externally, the bag is flanked by deep side gusset pockets specifically sized to secure a water bottle. Unzipping the main compartment reveals a camouflage-printed twill interior, outfitted with additional inner pockets to manage smaller items. Billed as a "One size fits all" carryall, the interior space is generous enough to house a 13-inch laptop alongside daily essentials. Arriving in muted, tactical-leaning "Black" and "Drab" variations, each unit comes stowed inside a custom drawstring bag finished with a screen-printed logo.The TELFAR "Utility Bag" drops on May 8 at 12 p.m. EST exclusively via TELFAR online, followed by an in-store release at its 408 Broadway flagship in New York City next week.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

A striking visual of a motorbike suspended mid-air against the sea serves as a central motif, creating a deliberate tension between movement and stillness. This atmosphere captures the underlying tension and unique rhythm of the Jamaican setting, where the environment itself feels like it shapes the evolving silhouettes.Staying true to the brand’s established DNA, key pieces from the latest seasonal range include oversized jackets, loose pants and washed tees, all presented in muted earth tones and sun‑bleached palettes that echo the campaign’s raw setting. Entertainment.title: Sunspel Celebrates 20 Years of the James Bond Riviera Polo With a Limited Sea Island Cotton Edition
Entertainment.text: SummarySunspel marks 20 years of the modern Riviera Polo with a limited Sea Island cotton editionThe release features the athletic silhouette tailored for Daniel Craig's James Bond in Casino RoyaleCrafted in signature navy, the $425 USD is now available to shopSunspel is celebrating two decades of its modern Riviera Polo Shirt with a prestigious limited-edition release that honors more than 160 years of British textile innovation. This 20th-anniversary edition marks the evolution of a design that originally traces back to the 1950s, when Peter Hill, the great-grandson of the brand's founder, engineered a breathable warp-knit cotton mesh for the French Riviera. The theme of this release centers on the intersection of heritage and cinematic history, specifically referencing the refined silhouette created in 2006 for Daniel Craig’s debut as James Bond in Casino Royale.The cornerstone of this commemorative release is the limited-edition Sea Island Cotton Riviera Polo, presented in Sunspel’s signature navy. While maintaining the streamlined, athletic fit and shortened sleeves of the 2006 silhouette, the material has been elevated to Sea Island cotton, a fiber prized since the 19th century for its exceptionally long staple length and natural lustre. This choice of fabric ensures a mood of understated luxury, as the cotton is celebrated for being the world's finest, producing a texture that is remarkably smooth, breathable and soft while retaining significant durability.Reflecting a commitment to uncompromising quality, each piece represents the brand's long-standing focus on innovative, high-quality natural materials. The polo’s refined handle and dry, subtly open structure remain central to the experience of the garment, offering superior comfort in warm climates.The 20th-anniversary Sea Island Cotton Riviera Polo is now available to shop through Sunspel, priced at $425 USD.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
